messages.text: What stops it from overheating or dying?

Great question — the Rev 6.1 has **three layers** working together:

**1. Spring-mounted heatsink + fan**
Presses evenly on all four BM1370 chips — no hot corner die. Result: ~57 °C at full 6 TH/s, quiet at ~40–45 dB.

**2. BSB custom airflow shroud**
Ducts cold air directly onto the **voltage regulators** — the part that silently kills most small miners first. Dedicated airflow keeps VRMs ~54 °C at full load.

**3. Upgraded power path (XT30 + thicker PCB)**
The old Rev 5 barrel jack sagged under load and cooked itself. Rev 6.1 uses a **15 A XT30 connector + 1 oz copper on 2 mm PCB** — input holds a stable 11.9 V at full speed, no brown-outs.

**Bonus — onboard F1 fuse:**
If there's a power spike, the small sacrificial fuse on the board takes the hit, not your miner electronics.

The included **350 W MeanWell PSU** runs at ~30% load feeding a ~100 W miner — cool, quiet, and long-lived by design.
